title: Fats Waller and Trombone Smitty at the Paradise
summary: Fats Waller's local band drank 52 fifths in a week, and Trombone Smitty brought the house down with one eight-bar bridge.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I also saw Fats Waller at the Paradise Theatre. Heh-heh, I can tell you something real funny about that. He came to Detroit with just his basic group, just the five pieces that he'd use all the time. Sedric... I don't remember the tenor player's name, but his last name was Sedric. [GENE SEDRIC] Anyway, that week he puts this local band together to play the engagement, and they drink 52 fifths of whiskey that week, the band! Yeah, he was responsible for the whiskey for the band, and he had a bunch of whiskey drinkers in that band!

But I did see one of the most phenomenal things that I have ever seen during that week that he was at the Paradise Theatre. There was a trombone player around Detroit, which most of the Jazz players claim that he was probably the best in the country at that time. But his temperament wasn't the greatest, and when he... He was a Jekyll and Hyde, when he was drinking and when he wasn't drinking; one of those people, you know. But this guy was a phenomenal trombone player, and he was a very good pianist also -- and his wife was a Classical piano teacher.
And they were playing some song, and Trombone Smitty played the bridge, the middle part -- eight bars he played. And everybody in this theatre just screamed. That's the
first time I've seen somebody play that small amount and get complete response from the audience. That was really something special. I'll always remember that scene, you know.
